goal: Pin down when/how the real ROS2 e2e trajectory diverges from PHYS-002's known physics-only trajectory, and whether that correlates with individual large jitter events (DIAG-001) or something else.

method.recorder: record_trajectory.py (extends DIAG-001's measure_jitter.py to also record actual q1/q2/tau1/tau2, using run_experiment.py's exact t0/_now_s() time-axis convention)
method.gain_used: original (pre-CTRL-006, currently deployed) -- same as PHYS-002's physics-only reference
method.physics_only_reference: tasks/PHYS-002-closed-loop-physics-only/evidence/physics_only_run_1.json (all 5 of that task's runs were bit-identical)

interpretation.single_big_jitter_event_hypothesis: NOT supported -- 0/4 runs show divergence onset near (within 0.2s of) that run's own single largest jitter event; some are over a second apart
interpretation.physics_only_settling_time_hypothesis: supported by clustering, not proven -- onset consistently lands 0.075-0.713s (mean 0.516s) after physics-only's own 3.24s settling moment, a much tighter and more consistent pattern than the largest-jitter-event timing (which spans 2.757-6.518s with no shared value across runs)
interpretation.plausible_mechanism: this gain is only marginally able to settle at all (PHYS-002/CTRL-006), and is likely most sensitive right around the moment it would otherwise cross into the settle band -- small, cumulative jitter (not one dramatic event) is enough to nudge it away from actually entering/staying in that band at that critical moment, and the marginal design doesn't recover once it misses
interpretation.caveat: plausible mechanism, not a proven one -- N=4 valid runs, one gain, one scenario
interpretation.null_result_reported: the lack of single-event correlation is reported as a real finding, not discarded or reframed to force a positive result

acceptance_checks.checked_against_physics_only_settling_ti: added beyond spec, because the numbers pointed there

next_step: Inject synthetic jitter (drawn from DIAG-001's measured distribution) into the physics-only harness's control period to test whether jitter alone (no other real-ROS2 confound) reproduces this same settle-then-diverge pattern -- would isolate jitter as sufficient. A gain search with an explicit delay/jitter-robustness objective (per CTRL-006) should specifically target robustness around the settling-boundary moment, per this task's finding.
